page: OVHcloud b3-640-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by AMD EPYC processors deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 160 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, configured with one thread per core. Memory capacity is set at 640 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps, with no integrated hardware accelerators or public IPv4 addresses bundled by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute capability, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng metric of 288,899.63 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 1,197.24 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Memory subsystems deliver 9,075.89 GB/sec in small-block cached read benchmarks and 282.47 GB/sec on large uncached read transfers. Single-core performance falls in the top 25 percent for raw CPU stress testing, while single-threaded compression tests place within the middle 50 percent. The instance also achieved 164.84 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 66.91 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation avoids hyperthreading contention, ensuring steady execution for high-concurrency tasks. However, the bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD represents a limited local storage footprint given the substantial processor and memory profile, necessitating external network block storage for capacity-heavy deployments. Given the high compute density and strong memory bandwidth, the instance is positioned for large-scale in-memory key-value stores, distributed software compilation, batch data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving architectures.

Local resources include 50 GB of NVMe SSD storage and a 20 Gbps baseline network interface, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark measurements reflect top-tier multi-core computing capability, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 288,899.63 and 164.84 million Redis SET operations per second. Although the 50 GB internal drive requires external storage planning for persistent data arrays, the dedicated single-thread-per-core configuration prevents hyperthread resource contention, making it suitable for distributed compilation, parallel batch processing, in-memory caching, and concurrent web tier workloads.
